title: I made a Pirate fantasy sequel game
author: l1vi
selftext:
Tales of Solaria is a 6 part fantasy series with expansive lore. Currently the materials are scattered everywhere but now with the help of Claude & NotebookLM for the lore, I am now able to adapt the materials into playable rpg games on [my main site](https://talesofsolaria.co.uk/games). This current game is a sequel to Act 2 of previous game I was working on.

The game can be played on single player and multiplayer (up to 3). There are plenty of mini games, interactive stories and there's a mystery brewing in the various kingdoms. Currently the game is in its beta phase as the pirate side of the story is in development.

comments.author: gholias
comments.body:
I'm going to give my honest opinion; don't be mad, okay?

I really, really hate AI-generated videos used to promote games. It's an automatic NOPE for me. Any game that uses an AI-generated video to promote itself, like the video in your post, gets ignored. I don't even look at whether the game is good or not, I just move on.

I believe those videos are part of the reason people hate anything AI-related in games.

But that's just my opinion, and I'm not sure if anyone else agrees.

replies.author: l1vi
replies.body: I understand. Thank you for you honesty, much better that what the other person commented

replies.author: mildmanneredme
replies.body: I agree. In this day and age with AI development, I think showing gameplay is a must now. Unless you're a triple A developer, you really cant get away with Non-gameplay footage.

replies.author: ponderdiggums
replies.body: Same here, they get an automatic no. We've seen so many titles in the mobile space  pre AI that had impressive promotional videos but zero to do with the actual gameplay. A promo AI video of a character doing a bunch of ninja moves is poor advertising for a game where you can't even jump.
